captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Kimi Antonelli
captains.reason: 40.1 avg points this season, topped FP2, won at Silverstone comfortably, fastest lap in 6 of 9 races. Unanimous consensus across all channels as the clear-cut 2x captain. Even with Hadjar's penalty upside, Antonelli's floor is higher and more reliable.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Isaac Hadjar
captains.reason: Starting P21/P22 due to back-of-grid engine penalty. Betting lines predict ~P8 finish, meaning 13-14 positions gained plus massive overtake points. Multiple channels flag him as potential Autopilot chip candidate to challenge Antonelli's score. Five straight top-6 finishes. Red Bull looked strong in FP1 (P4) and FP2 (P5).

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Charles Leclerc
captains.reason: Cheapest A-tier driver, strong favored-driver bias for Driver of the Day. Good 4-race setup option paired with Antonelli. ZachGP highlights him as the meta shift differential for budget builders. However, was 8/10ths off Hamilton in FP2 — needs to find pace.

buy.name: Isaac Hadjar
buy.note: Back-of-grid penalty creates one of the biggest B-tier scoring opportunities of the season. Five straight top-6 finishes. FanAmp says 'do whatever it takes to get him in your lineup.' All channels agree he is the must-have B-tier asset this week.

buy.name: Gabriel Bortoleto
buy.note: Needs only 3 points for max 0.6M price rise. P10 in FP1. Audi brought Spa-spec rear wing. Consistent scorer and strong budget builder. Multiple channels recommend swapping Hulkenberg for Bortoleto this week.

buy.name: Arvid Lindblad
buy.note: Needs just 1 point for max 0.6M price rise. No negative points since Canada (5 races ago). Racing Bulls look strong at Spa. ZachGP's favorite budget pick. P9 in FP2.

consider.name: Franco Colapinto
consider.note: Needs only 1 point for max 0.6M price rise (-8 for minimum rise). Best price thresholds of any B-tier driver. Was quicker Alpine in FP1/FP2. FanAmp and F1FantasyPolePosition both highlight him. However, Alpine were P15 in FP1 — less inspiring than Racing Bulls/Audi.

consider.name: Liam Lawson
consider.note: Consistent scorer needing 6 points for max rise. Racing Bulls entrenched in top 10 both practice sessions. May be the sacrifice to fund double premium constructors but still a strong hold. FormulaFantasyHub notes 6 points is 'very easily attainable' for Lawson.

consider.name: Esteban Ocon
consider.note: One of only two drivers (with Hamilton) to score 7+ points in every race this season. 6.4 overtakes per race. Needs only 2 points for 0.2M rise. Good consolation if 0.1M short of Colapinto.

consider.name: Ollie Bearman
consider.note: No reliability issues since Monaco. Consistent points scorer. 3.1M cheaper than Ocon. ZachGP rates him alongside Lindblad and Bortoleto as top budget trio. Needs 6 points for minimum rise — tighter threshold than others.

consider.name: Red Bull Constructor
consider.note: Verstappen topped FP1, Hadjar P4. Removed problematic 'Macarena wing.' Hadjar's back-of-grid start means huge overtake/positions-gained points for constructor too. FanAmp calls it 'a great differential play.' FormulaFantasyHub notes it as a viable swap from Ferrari for teams that can't afford Hadjar as a driver.

avoid: Fernando Alonso — Goal is to 'get home to watch Spain in the World Cup final.' Aston Martin upgrades not until Hungary. Multiple channels say wait one more week.
Lance Stroll — 3M price floor but 'lives and breathes P22.' DNFs in 3 of last 4 races. Not a points source even with grid penalty.
Sergio Perez — Reliability concerns, no fantasy upside.
Alex Albon — Not competitive enough for his price.
Carlos Sainz — Not competitive enough for his price.
Pierre Gasly — 13M price tag too expensive relative to Hadjar at similar price. Heavy crash in FP2, car damage. Alpine not inspiring on pace.

Lando Norris — Only 10-place grid penalty, not enough overtake upside to justify 2x or Final Fix. FanAmp ran the numbers: best-case ~30 pts on Sunday vs Antonelli's typical ~35. Betting lines predict P7 finish. All channels agree he is NOT a viable 2x candidate.

chips.name: Autopilot
chips.reason: Multiple channels (FanAmp, F1FantasyPolePosition, FormulaFantasyHub) flag this as a strong Autopilot week. With Hadjar starting P21/P22 and potentially challenging Antonelli's score, Autopilot lets you hedge between Antonelli 2x and Hadjar 2x. FormulaFantasyHub explicitly titles their video 'USE AUTOPILOT THIS WEEK.' Best used if you have both Antonelli and Hadjar in your squad.

chips.name: Final Fix
chips.reason: FanAmp ran detailed analysis on using Final Fix to swap in Norris on Sunday — concluded it's not worth it. Norris's ceiling with a 10-place penalty (~30 pts best case) doesn't exceed a typical Antonelli Sunday (~35 pts). Save for a true emergency. Note: using Autopilot locks you out of Final Fix for the weekend.

chips.name: No Negative
chips.reason: FanAmp notes No Negative is 'always in play at Spa' due to the track's history of incidents and DNFs. However, DNFs have calmed down this season according to ZachGP. Consider if you're running risky assets or reliability-prone cars.

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: No channel recommends using Wildcard this week. The meta transition to 4A lineups is not yet optimal — F1 Fantasy Tools sims and multiple channels suggest holding off one more week until Hungary when Aston Martin bring upgrades and the picture is clearer.

watch_items: George Russell was 1.2 seconds off Antonelli in FP2 qualifying sims — needs to find grip overnight. If he doesn't solve it, Mercedes constructor value drops and Red Bull becomes more attractive.
Charles Leclerc was nearly 8/10ths behind Hamilton in FP2 — Ferrari constructor could be weaker if the gap persists into qualifying.
Oscar Piastri suffered a late hydraulic pressure issue in FP1 — monitor McLaren reliability.
Pierre Gasly crashed heavily in FP2 bringing out a red flag — Alpine expect him back Saturday but car damage extent unclear.
Red Bull removed the 'Macarena wing' that reportedly led to Verstappen's recent retirements — Verstappen looked more comfortable and topped FP1.
Audi brought a Spa-specification rear wing — both Hulkenberg and Bortoleto expected to compete around top 10.
Weather: 25% chance of rain on Sunday, cooling temperatures through the weekend. Spa's microclimate means conditions can change rapidly.
Exact grid penalty order: Hadjar (back of grid), Norris (10 places), and Stroll (penalty) — final starting positions affect overtake scoring calculations.
Aston Martin upgrades confirmed for Hungary (next race), NOT Spa — factor into multi-race planning.
arc: Spa is the final race before Hungary, which is shaping up as a major inflection point. Aston Martin are bringing upgrades to the Hungaroring (where they were 3rd-best team in 2025), potentially making Alonso/Stroll viable again. Multiple channels note that the transition to 4A lineups (4 premium drivers) is approaching but not yet optimal — F1 Fantasy Tools sims suggest holding off one more week. Hungary is also a track where Verstappen historically excels, and the overtaking dynamics with new 2026 regs are unknown, making it a potential shake-up. For now, the strategy is to maximize budget building at Spa through Hadjar's penalty-fueled scoring and cheap B-tier price rises (Lindblad, Bortoleto, Colapinto all needing ~1 point for max rises), then reassess the meta for Hungary with upgraded Aston Martin data and clearer constructor pecking order.
